He says COP31 brought together global leaders, policymakers, scientists, development partners, business representatives and civil society organisations under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), to strengthen collaboration and turn climate commitments into tangible action. The column begins its account of traditional adaptation with courtyard homes, porches, shaded transition areas, nearby materials and climate-conscious building orientations, and illustrates climate-resilient housing with a BRAC-built house for poor people in coastal areas. stories.exam_facts: The agreement was signed by Gitanjali Singh, Representative of UN Women, and Ivo Freijsen, Representative of UNHCR, and establishes a framework for cooperation through 2028. The collaboration will focus on further integrating gender equality and protection into humanitarian planning and services; increasing women's representation and participation in camp governance and decision-making; enhancing support for Rohingya women-led groups; and expanding opportunities for education, skills development, livelihoods and leadership. UNHCR and UN Women will work with humanitarian actors, government counterparts, refugee volunteers and community leaders to strengthen capacities on refugee protection and gender equality, challenge harmful gender norms and promote positive masculinities, and jointly advocate for policies and programmes responding to the needs of women, girls, men and boys. The signing comes during the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence, and follows the recent International Court of Justice ruling on The Gambia vs Myanmar, after which the agencies echoed the UN Secretary-General's statement. The MoU builds on the two agencies' long-standing partnership and supports the Global Compact on Refugees and the Inter-Agency Standing Committee's Gender Equality and Women's Empowerment Agenda.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman said Bangladesh should become a trusted brand in the global livestock market. Inaugurating National Livestock Week 2026 in Dhaka on 26 November, he listed halal meat, dairy, poultry and leather goods as exports. Milk, meat and eggs supply 56% of the country's animal protein, and about 15 lakh marginal farmers depend on livestock. The government is building modern processing centres and disease-free zones and enforcing international quarantine standards to make the sector a major foreign-currency earner, a livestock-export hook for BCS/Bank.

He also distributed the National Livestock Awards 2026 at the inauguration, held at the old Trade Fair Ground in Dhaka.

stories.headline: Deputy Speaker calls for amending Article 70, independent Parliament Secretariat
stories.summary: Deputy Speaker Kayesar Kamal on 26 November called for amending Article 70 so MPs can vote independently. He wants safeguards on matters of national interest, and an independent Parliament Secretariat under Article 79. He also urged a law under Article 76(3) to make standing committees effective scrutineers of the executive. The call came at a Dhaka seminar on making the Jatiya Sangsad efficient, after parliaments that became rubber stamps for the executive, a constitutional-reform hook for BCS/Bank.
stories.exam_facts: Kamal named Articles 70, 76, 77 and 79 of the Constitution as requiring attention. Political scientist Professor Rounaq Jahan said many of the reforms being discussed had already been recommended in a 2012 study on Parliament but few had been implemented, and she urged a parliamentary code of conduct, annual disclosure of MPs' financial assets and declarations of conflicts of interest. Saiful Alam Milan, a Jamaat-e-Islami leader and MP from Dhaka-12, said 94 bills were passed in 25 working days during the first session, two civil service bills in eight minutes without discussion, and the Invest Bangladesh Bill on the same day it was approved by the Cabinet, without scrutiny by a parliamentary committee. The seminar, 'How Can the Jatiya Sangsad Be Made More Efficient and Effective', was organised by Dhaka Tribune with the support of the Royal Norwegian Embassy.

stories.headline: Bangladesh needs to rethink how power lines cross its major rivers
stories.summary: Columnist Md Azizur Rahman argues Bangladesh must rethink how power lines cross its major rivers. He proposes shared transmission corridors where several lines cross the same river. Power Grid Bangladesh PLC, the sole national transmission utility, runs the high-voltage network at 132 kV, 230 kV and 400 kV, and each river crossing without a corridor becomes a huge maritime construction job of crane barges, tugboats and dredging. stories.headline: Dhaka Elevated Expressway: 81pc completed, Panthakunja ramp likely to open soon, Kamalapur section by June
stories.summary: Eighty-one per cent of the Dhaka Elevated Expressway is complete, the Bangladesh Bridge Authority says, with the Panthakunja ramp targeted to open next January and the Kamalapur section by June next year. The government has paid over Tk 10.68 billion to the investor in the first and second instalments, and the construction company will collect tolls for 25 years, with the government receiving a share of toll revenue. It is the country's first elevated expressway, implemented by the Bangladesh Bridge Authority, and the First Dhaka Elevated Expressway (FDEE) Company Limited was formed to construct and operate it.

stories.summary: State Minister Humaiun Kobir said on 26 November that India is realising Sheikh Hasina is a thorn in Bangladesh-India relations. stories.headline: It's not possible to shut down all brick kilns, but the most harmful ones must be closed first: Martin Mattsson
stories.summary: Martin Mattsson says it is not possible to shut down all brick kilns, but the most harmful ones must be closed first, and his Brick Kiln Tracker ranks them by health harm. He estimates Bangladesh loses 5.5 years of life expectancy to air pollution — the world’s worst (Air Quality Life Index 2025), with kilns’ share of Dhaka’s fine-particle pollution at about a tenth to over half. He argues hollow concrete blocks, which need no firing, could replace most bricks within a few years, an environment-and-health hook for BCS/Bank.
stories.exam_facts: The Brick Kiln Tracker was built from satellite data, machine learning and air-quality modelling: a neural network scans high-resolution satellite images, a person checks every kiln and records its technology (zigzag or fixed-chimney) and whether it operated that season, and a second machine-learning model tracks active kilns from lower-resolution imagery updated more frequently. The current tracker is based on kilns active in the 2025/26 brick kiln season. Mattsson stresses the health estimates are modelled, not measured, and the total number of deaths caused by kilns is therefore uncertain, though the ranking of kilns is more reliable because the same assumptions apply to every kiln. Mattsson is Assistant Professor in the Department of Economics at the National University of Singapore, interviewed by Partha Shankar Saha.

stories.headline: Why climate advocacy must move from protest to practical action
stories.summary: Columnist Bidhan Chandra Pal argues climate advocacy must move from protest to practical action. He says success is measured not by how loudly demands are expressed but by how effectively they become lasting change. Writing on 26 November, he notes a persistent gap between international climate commitments and implementation, citing the UN Environment Programme's Emissions Gap Report, which shows current policies remain insufficient to meet the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C temperature goal, a climate-policy hook for BCS/Bank.
stories.exam_facts: Pal lists the core negotiation issues as historical responsibility, emissions reduction, climate finance, adaptation, loss and damage, technology transfer and the protection of vulnerable populations. He says peaceful protest remains a legitimate and necessary form of civic participation, and his objective is to complement traditional advocacy with practical solutions, meaningful partnerships and stronger engagement in implementation, not to abandon protest or weaken accountability. He argues stronger partnerships can turn local solutions into wider climate initiatives.

stories.headline: Gazipur workers clash with police over new wages, 30 factories declare holiday
stories.summary: Garment workers clashed with police in Gazipur for a second consecutive day on 26 November. They rejected the wage board's new pay structure; at least 30 factories declared a holiday. Workers blocked the Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways around 11:30 am, set fire to rubbish on the road, vandalised a police motorcycle and briefly held an industrial police inspector captive before he was rescued. Police, Border Guard Bangladesh and Ansar dispersed them with tear gas, sound grenades and batons, while 32 factories closed indefinitely stayed shut, a labour-unrest hook for BCS/Bank.
stories.exam_facts: Protests also broke out in Sreepur, where workers blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway at about 11:30 am, and three days' leave was announced at several factories in Bagher Bazar and Bhabanipur in Gazipur Sadar upazila. Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Amzad Hossain confirmed the incident, saying a police motorcycle had been vandalised. Businessman Akbar Ali said outsiders had joined the workers and attacked the police. The protests follow the 25 November announcement of a Tk 17,000 minimum wage, after workers had demanded Tk 30,000.

words.Original example: However, the growing use of plastic packaging, rising waste generation and resource consumption have also created significant environmental challenges.
words.Newspaper context note: The FMCG editorial says plastic packaging is a major source of waste and environmental harm.
words.Article headline: Sustainability of FMCG sector
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Everyday business and environment word for BCS/Bank comprehension; links to recycling and export topics.

words.English definition: Working together with another person or organisation to achieve something.
words.Collocations / patterns: deepen collaboration; international collaboration; collaboration between agencies
words.Original example: The collaboration will focus on further integrating gender equality and protection into humanitarian planning and services; increasing women's representation and participation in camp governance and decision-making; enhancing support for Rohingya women-led groups; and expanding opportunities for education, skills development, livelihoods and leadership.
words.Newspaper context note: UN Women and UNHCR will work together to make the Rohingya response more gender-responsive and inclusive.
words.Article headline: UN Women and UNHCR deepen collaboration for a more inclusive Rohingya refugee response
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Core BCS/Bank word for international affairs, UN and development passages; 'collaborate/collaboration' is a frequent test item.

words.English definition: A relationship in which two or more people or organisations work together, sharing aims and responsibilities.
words.Collocations / patterns: long-standing partnership; strategic partnership; public-private partnership
words.Original example: The MoU builds on the long-standing partnership between the two agencies.
words.Newspaper context note: The UN Women-UNHCR agreement continues a partnership the two agencies have had for years.
words.Article headline: UN Women and UNHCR deepen collaboration for a more inclusive Rohingya refugee response
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Standard BCS/Bank word for diplomacy, trade and development; 'public-private partnership' and 'strategic partnership' are set phrases.

words.English definition: Depending too much on one thing, person or source, so that problems follow if it fails.
words.Collocations / patterns: overreliance on garments; overreliance on one market; overreliance on exports
words.Original example: Bangladesh, meanwhile, remains constrained by regulatory uncertainty, weak infrastructure and an overreliance on garments.
words.Newspaper context note: The analysis says Bangladesh is held back by depending too heavily on garment exports.
words.Article headline: What Vietnam got right, and Bangladesh missed
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Key economics word for BCS/Bank essays and comprehension on exports and trade; pairs with 'diversification'.

words.English definition: The state of being sure about something, or a fact known to be true; the predictability that investors and businesses can trust.
words.Collocations / patterns: offer certainty; fall in love with certainty; policy certainty
words.Original example: It falls in love with certainty.
words.Newspaper context note: The columnist argues that global capital is drawn to predictability: Vietnam offered certainty, Bangladesh offered uncertainty. The fuller passage reads: 'Global capital does not fall in love with communism or capitalism. It falls in love with certainty.'
words.Article headline: What Vietnam got right, and Bangladesh missed
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Core BCS/Bank word for economy and investment passages; the 'certain/certainty/uncertainty' family is frequently tested.

words.English definition: The separate parts from which a machine, product or system is made.
words.Collocations / patterns: electronic components; components and parts; key components
words.Original example: Computers, electronics, and components alone earned $107.75 billion last year, nearly a quarter of its exports, with Samsung generating roughly one in every eight export dollars.
words.Newspaper context note: Vietnam earns nearly a quarter of its exports from computers, electronics and components.
words.Article headline: What Vietnam got right, and Bangladesh missed
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Useful BCS/Bank word for trade, industry and technology passages; 'electronic components' is a set phrase.

words.English definition: Connected with the sea, ships or shipping.
words.Collocations / patterns: maritime construction; maritime safety; maritime boundary
words.Original example: Where no such corridor exists, every river crossing effectively becomes a massive maritime construction operation.
words.Newspaper context note: Without a bridge corridor, building power lines across a river becomes a huge operation on the water, using barges and boats.
words.Article headline: Bangladesh needs to rethink how power lines cross its major rivers
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Important BCS/Bank adjective for geography, blue economy and defence passages; 'maritime boundary' and 'maritime safety' are exam phrases.

words.English definition: A period during which animals, people or goods are kept apart to stop a disease from spreading, or the rules for doing so.
words.Collocations / patterns: quarantine standards; international quarantine; quarantine rules
words.Original example: Tarique said strict compliance with international quarantine standards was essential to exporting livestock and animal-based products.
words.Newspaper context note: Bangladesh must meet international quarantine rules before it can export meat, dairy and other animal products.
words.Article headline: PM seeks to make Bangladesh a trusted brand in global livestock market
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Key word for BCS/Bank agriculture, livestock and public-health questions; a common exam word since the pandemic.

words.English definition: The introduction of semen into an animal to cause pregnancy, especially artificial insemination in livestock breeding.
words.Collocations / patterns: artificial insemination; insemination services; cattle insemination
words.Original example: He stressed increasing productivity through modern technology, improved breeds, artificial insemination, vaccination, quality feed and better farm management.
words.Newspaper context note: The prime minister listed modern breeding methods among the ways to raise livestock productivity.
words.Article headline: PM seeks to make Bangladesh a trusted brand in global livestock market
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Agriculture and livestock vocabulary for BCS/Bank; 'artificial insemination' is a set technical phrase.

words.English definition: The food and substances the body needs to stay healthy and grow, and the study of how food affects health.
words.Collocations / patterns: food and nutrition security; good nutrition; nutrition security
words.Original example: The prime minister said livestock contributed to food and nutrition security, employment generation, poverty reduction and rural economic development.
words.Newspaper context note: Livestock helps feed the country: milk, meat and eggs supply over half of Bangladesh's animal protein.
words.Article headline: PM seeks to make Bangladesh a trusted brand in global livestock market
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Core BCS/Bank word for health, food security and development questions; 'nutrition security' is a standard phrase.

words.English definition: The act of watching and checking that people or organisations do their work properly, especially a parliament checking the government.
words.Collocations / patterns: parliamentary oversight; oversight of the executive; strengthen oversight
words.Original example: She said MPs should prioritise national legislation and oversight instead of focusing mainly on development projects in their constituencies.
words.Newspaper context note: A political scientist says MPs should spend more time making laws and checking the government than on local projects.
words.Article headline: Deputy Speaker calls for amending Article 70, independent Parliament Secretariat
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Central BCS/Bank word for parliament, constitution and governance questions; often confused with 'an oversight' meaning a mistake.

words.English definition: The way a country, organisation or system is governed and managed, including its rules and institutions.
words.Collocations / patterns: democratic governance; good governance; corporate governance
words.Original example: The event brought together policymakers, political representatives, academics and experts to discuss parliamentary institutions, democratic governance and accountability.
words.Newspaper context note: A seminar in Dhaka discussed how to make parliament more effective, covering institutions, governance and accountability.
words.Article headline: Deputy Speaker calls for amending Article 70, independent Parliament Secretariat
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Core BCS/Bank word for polity, administration and development; 'good governance' is a standard exam topic.

words.English definition: A sloping road or path that joins a higher road, such as an expressway, to a lower one.
words.Collocations / patterns: down ramp; expressway ramp; entry ramp
words.Original example: The section from Kawla to Farmgate was opened to traffic on 3 September 2023, while the down ramp adjacent to the FDC rail gate was opened on 20 March 2024.
words.Newspaper context note: Parts of the Dhaka Elevated Expressway and its ramps have opened in stages since September 2023.
words.Article headline: Dhaka Elevated Expressway: 81pc completed, Panthakunja ramp likely to open soon, Kamalapur section by June
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Infrastructure vocabulary for BCS/Bank; useful in passages on roads, expressways and transport projects.

words.English definition: The state of being crowded or blocked, especially with too much traffic on a road.
words.Collocations / patterns: traffic congestion; reduce congestion; congestion charge
words.Original example: The expressway is being constructed from Kawla, south of the airport, to Kutubkhali on the Dhaka-Chattogram Highway, with the aim of reducing traffic congestion in the capital.
words.Newspaper context note: The Dhaka Elevated Expressway is being built to reduce traffic congestion in the capital.
words.Article headline: Dhaka Elevated Expressway: 81pc completed, Panthakunja ramp likely to open soon, Kamalapur section by June
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Core BCS/Bank word for passages on urbanisation, transport and infrastructure; common in newspaper reporting on Dhaka traffic.

words.English definition: Possible to do easily or conveniently; able to be achieved with the available time and resources.
words.Collocations / patterns: technically feasible; economically feasible; feasible within a few years
words.Original example: Concrete blocks are widely used both around the world and in Bangladesh, and switching most construction to using concrete blocks is feasible within just a few years if we start today.
words.Newspaper context note: A researcher says Bangladesh could switch most building from fired bricks to concrete blocks within a few years.
words.Article headline: It's not possible to shut down all brick kilns, but the most harmful ones must be closed first: Martin Mattsson
words.BCS / Bank relevance: High-frequency BCS/Bank adjective for comprehension and writing; the 'feasible/feasibility' pair is a common test item.

words.English definition: Allowed by law or rules, or accepted as right and reasonable.
words.Collocations / patterns: legitimate protest; legitimate concern; legitimate demand
words.Original example: Peaceful protest remains a legitimate and necessary form of civic participation.
words.Newspaper context note: The columnist says peaceful protest is a lawful and necessary part of civic life, even while urging climate action to become more practical.
words.Article headline: Why climate advocacy must move from protest to practical action
words.BCS / Bank relevance: Core BCS/Bank adjective for law, polity and comprehension; 'legitimacy' is a standard governance topic.

revision_words.English definition: Money sent home by a person working abroad, usually to their family.
revision_words.Synonyms: money transfer; foreign earnings; overseas income
revision_words.Collocations / patterns: remittance houses; remittance inflows; send remittances; formal remittances
revision_words.Original example: Following the auction, remittance houses lowered their dollar selling rates to below Tk125, from Tk125.30-Tk125.40 earlier in the day, easing pressure on the exchange rate.
revision_words.Newspaper context note: Remittance houses cut their dollar rates below Tk125 after Bangladesh Bank sold $205 million.
revision_words.Article headline: Bangladesh Bank sells $205m to banks, dollar rate falls below Tk125
revision_words.BCS / Bank relevance: Core BCS/Bank economy vocabulary — remittance is central to reserves, the exchange rate and the balance of payments.

revision_words.Bangla meaning: ঘাটতি; আয় থেকে ব্যয় বেশি হওয়া
revision_words.English definition: The amount by which spending is greater than income, especially in a government budget.
revision_words.Collocations / patterns: budget deficit; fiscal deficit; trade deficit; cover the deficit
revision_words.Original example: For years, the government covered part of its budget deficit by borrowing from the central bank, which in plain terms means creating new money.
revision_words.Newspaper context note: The columnists argue deficit financing by borrowing from the central bank weakened the taka.
revision_words.Article headline: Fixing the taka means fixing the budget, banks, and exports
revision_words.BCS / Bank relevance: BCS/Bank economy vocabulary — budget and fiscal deficits are standard written-topic words.

revision_words.Bangla meaning: অতিমুদ্রাস্ফীতি; অতি দ্রুত ও অনিয়ন্ত্রিত মূল্যবৃদ্ধি
revision_words.English definition: Extremely rapid and out-of-control inflation, with prices rising very fast.
revision_words.Synonyms: runaway inflation; galloping inflation; price explosion
revision_words.Collocations / patterns: decades of hyperinflation; hyperinflation crisis; suffer hyperinflation
revision_words.Original example: Brazil suffered decades of hyperinflation, large deficits and a constantly sinking currency.
revision_words.Newspaper context note: Brazil's decades of hyperinflation are cited as a comparative case for the taka.
revision_words.Article headline: Fixing the taka means fixing the budget, banks, and exports
revision_words.BCS / Bank relevance: BCS/Bank economy vocabulary — hyperinflation is a classic advanced term in monetary economics.

revision_words.Bangla meaning: অবমূল্যায়ন করা; মুদ্রার সরকারি মান কমানো
revision_words.English definition: To officially reduce the value of a currency against other currencies.
revision_words.Synonyms: depreciate; downgrade; lower the value of
revision_words.Collocations / patterns: devalue the currency; devalued in steps; devaluation of the taka
revision_words.Original example: It devalued in steps, moved from a fixed rate to a market-determined one, cut tariffs, scrapped rigid licensing, attracted deposits and remittances from overseas Indians and pushed exports beyond traditional commodities.
revision_words.Newspaper context note: India devalued in steps during its 1991 crisis, the columnists write.
revision_words.Article headline: Fixing the taka means fixing the budget, banks, and exports
revision_words.BCS / Bank relevance: BCS/Bank economy vocabulary — devaluation is a standard exchange-rate term.

revision_words.Bangla meaning: অরক্ষিত; বিনিময় হারের ঝুঁকি থেকে সুরক্ষাহীন
revision_words.English definition: (Of borrowing or an investment) not protected against the risk of exchange-rate or price movements.
revision_words.Collocations / patterns: unhedged dollar borrowing; unhedged foreign borrowing; unhedged exposure
revision_words.Original example: Third, banks need serious repair: independent reviews of loan quality, firm action against willful defaulters, stronger capital requirements and strict limits on unhedged dollar borrowing by companies, so the next depreciation does not wreck their balance sheets.
revision_words.Newspaper context note: The columnists urge strict limits on unhedged dollar borrowing by companies.
revision_words.Article headline: Fixing the taka means fixing the budget, banks, and exports
revision_words.BCS / Bank relevance: BCS/Bank banking vocabulary — hedging is a key concept in foreign-exchange risk.

phrases.Bangla meaning: নামমাত্র অনুমোদনকারী সংস্থা; যা শুধু সিল মারে, আসল ক্ষমতা নেই
phrases.English explanation: A person or body that formally approves decisions made by someone else without really examining them or having any real power.
phrases.Usage / register: Formal, political and parliamentary reporting; often critical.
phrases.Original example 1: Speaking at a seminar in Dhaka on Thursday, he said Bangladesh’s parliamentary history had seen both democratic progress and serious setbacks, with some parliaments strengthening democratic institutions while others had weakened them and become rubber stamps for the executive.
phrases.Original example 2: Saiful Alam Milan, a member central executive committee of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami and a lawmaker from Dhaka-12, said the July uprising had created an opportunity to rebuild Parliament after 15 years of authoritarian rule, during which elections lost credibility and the legislature largely became a rubber stamp for government decisions.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: become a rubber stamp; a rubber-stamp parliament; rubber-stamp approval
phrases.Article headline: Deputy Speaker calls for amending Article 70, independent Parliament Secretariat
phrases.Exam value: High-value BCS/Bank idiom for parliament and governance passages; a classic metaphor for a powerless legislature.

phrases.English explanation: As one piece or element of something larger, such as an agreement or programme.
phrases.Original example 1: As part of the agreement, UNHCR and UN Women will work with humanitarian actors, government counterparts, refugee volunteers and community leaders to strengthen their capacities on refugee protection and gender equality, challenge harmful gender norms and promote positive masculinities, and jointly advocate for policies and programmes that respond to the needs of women, girls, men and boys.
phrases.Original example 2: As part of the pilot phase of the Family Card Programme, a total of 74,259 families had been brought under the allowance scheme by September.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: as part of the agreement; as part of a programme; as part of the plan
phrases.Article headline: UN Women and UNHCR deepen collaboration for a more inclusive Rohingya refugee response
phrases.Exam value: High-frequency BCS/Bank phrase for comprehension and translation; used in agreements, programmes and official statements.

phrases.English explanation: To rely on someone or something, or to be decided by something.
phrases.Original example 1: Around 15 lakh marginal farmers also depend on livestock rearing for their livelihoods, he said, stressing the need for better veterinary treatment and disease prevention services.
phrases.Original example 2: Such measures depend on decisions by individual states and international institutions.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: depend on something; depend on someone for support; it depends on
phrases.Article headline: PM seeks to make Bangladesh a trusted brand in global livestock market
phrases.Exam value: Core BCS/Bank phrasal verb for comprehension and grammar; 'depend on' (not 'depend of') is a classic preposition test.

phrases.English explanation: A deal between two or more countries to reduce or remove tariffs and other barriers so goods can be traded more freely.
phrases.Original example 1: It has 17 free trade agreements in force covering over 60 economies.
phrases.Original example 2: Bangladesh has no major free trade agreement in operation.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: sign a free trade agreement; a free trade agreement in force; bilateral free trade agreement
phrases.Article headline: What Vietnam got right, and Bangladesh missed
phrases.Exam value: Central BCS/Bank trade term; Vietnam's 17 FTAs versus Bangladesh's none is a live exam comparison.

phrases.English explanation: Working together between countries on defence matters such as equipment, training, technology and security.
phrases.Original example 1: The agreement was reached at the 14th meeting of the India-UAE Joint Defence Cooperation Committee (JDCC) in Abu Dhabi yesterday.
phrases.Original example 2: The two sides also agreed to review progress in defence cooperation at regular intervals before the next JDCC meeting.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: Joint Defence Cooperation Committee; expand defence cooperation; defence cooperation agreement
phrases.Article headline: India, UAE agree to speed up joint development of defence equipment
phrases.Exam value: Key BCS/Bank international-affairs collocation; the India-UAE JDCC is a current example.

phrases.English explanation: The idea that the burdens and benefits of climate change should be shared fairly, with vulnerable countries and communities protected.
phrases.Original example 1: Through demonstrations, campaigns and international climate conferences, activists have brought climate change and climate justice to the centre of global debate.
phrases.Original example 2: These issues remain fundamental to climate justice.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: climate justice and gender justice; fight for climate justice; climate justice for vulnerable countries
phrases.Article headline: Why climate advocacy must move from protest to practical action
phrases.Exam value: Core BCS/Bank climate term; links climate change, COP31 and gender in exam questions.

phrases.English explanation: Making goods in a way that protects the environment, uses resources carefully and can continue for a long time.
phrases.Original example 1: As global markets increasingly shift towards sustainable production, adoption of green business practices is becoming not only an environmental responsibility but also an economic opportunity for Bangladesh.
phrases.Original example 2: Beyond the domestic market, sustainable production offers significant export opportunities.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: shift towards sustainable production; sustainable production practices; sustainable production and consumption
phrases.Exam value: Key BCS/Bank environment and economy collocation; ties FMCG, exports and green business together.

phrases.English explanation: Money in the currency of another country, earned through exports or held in reserves.
phrases.Original example 1: Such diversification could reduce dependence on traditional export sectors and create new sources of foreign currency.
phrases.Original example 2: The government was working to establish modern processing centres and disease-free zones to boost exports and make the sector a major source of foreign currency.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: earn foreign currency; a source of foreign currency; foreign currency reserves
phrases.Exam value: Central BCS/Bank economics term; appears in export, remittance and reserve questions.

phrases.English explanation: Harmful smoke, dust and gases in the air that damage health and the environment.
phrases.Usage / register: Neutral to formal, environment and health reporting.
phrases.Original example 1: At the same time, major cities such as Dhaka and Chattogram are grappling with the consequences of uncontrolled urban growth, wetland encroachment, shrinking green spaces, traffic congestion, air pollution and rising urban temperatures.
phrases.Original example 2: Bangladesh loses more life expectancy to air pollution than any other country: 5.5 years for the average person (Air Quality Life Index, 2025).
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: air pollution crisis; air pollution in Dhaka; reduce air pollution
phrases.Article headline: Building a climate-resilient Bangladesh: The role of architecture beyond COP31
phrases.Exam value: Core BCS/Bank environment term; the 5.5-year life-expectancy figure is directly exam-askable.

phrases.English explanation: The companies and factories that design and make military equipment and weapons.
phrases.Original example 1: To facilitate business-to-business (B2B) partnerships, a delegation from the Indian defence industry accompanied the JDCC delegation.
phrases.Original example 2: The Indian defence industry delegation visited Tawazun Industrial Park and met the Tawazun Economic Council in the UAE to explore potential areas of mutual cooperation with their Emirati counterparts.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: defence industry delegation; defence industry cooperation; the Indian defence industry
phrases.Article headline: India, UAE agree to speed up joint development of defence equipment
phrases.Exam value: Useful BCS/Bank international-affairs collocation; appears in India-UAE defence and trade stories.

mcqs.question: What does “intrusion” mean in the sentence about saltwater intrusion?

options.A: A sudden attack by an army
options.B: The unwanted entry of something harmful into a place
options.C: A formal introduction at a meeting

mcqs.explanation: Saltwater intrusion is seawater entering coastal land and water where it does not belong; the word means an unwanted entry, not an attack or an introduction.

mcqs.question: In the phrase “translating climate commitments into tangible action”, what does “tangible” mean?

options.B: Secret and hidden from the public
options.C: Real and practical, able to be seen or achieved

mcqs.explanation: Tangible action is real, practical action that can be seen and measured, as opposed to mere promises.

mcqs.question: What does “diversification” mean?

options.A: Reducing the number of products a country sells
options.B: Depending on a single export item
options.D: Spreading trade and production across many different products and markets

mcqs.explanation: Diversification means spreading across many products and markets so a country does not depend on one export, as the editorial recommends for Bangladesh.

mcqs.question: What does “overreliance” mean in the sentence about Bangladesh and garments?

options.B: A strong, balanced and fast-growing economy
options.C: Careful long-term planning by the government
options.D: A new trade deal signed with a neighbour

mcqs.explanation: Overreliance means depending too much on one thing; here Bangladesh depends too heavily on garment exports.

mcqs.question: In the sentence “Computers, electronics, and components alone earned $107.75 billion”, what are “components”?

options.C: Parts used to make a larger product
options.D: Workers employed in the big export factories

mcqs.explanation: Components are the parts used to build a larger product, such as the parts inside computers and electronics.

mcqs.question: What does “maritime” mean?

options.A: Relating to the sea and ships
options.B: Relating to mountains and high land
options.C: Relating to deserts and dry weather
options.D: Relating to forests and wild animals

mcqs.explanation: Maritime means connected with the sea and ships; the article calls river-crossing work a maritime construction operation because it happens on the water.

mcqs.question: What does “quarantine” mean in the livestock story?

options.A: A special tax charged on imported meat and milk
options.B: A festival held for farmers every year
options.C: A new breed of cattle developed by scientists
options.D: Keeping animals apart to stop disease

mcqs.explanation: Quarantine means keeping animals apart, or following rules to do so, to stop disease spreading; meeting international quarantine standards is essential for livestock exports.

mcqs.question: What does “oversight” mean in the parliament story?

options.C: A small mistake made by accident
options.D: A long speech given by a minister in parliament

mcqs.explanation: Oversight is parliament watching and checking the government's work; MPs are urged to prioritise legislation and oversight.

mcqs.question: In the sentence about the Dhaka Elevated Expressway, what does “congestion” mean?

options.A: Too much traffic blocking the roads
options.B: The construction of a new road through a crowded city area
options.C: The toll charged on an expressway
options.D: A new ramp joining a highway

mcqs.explanation: Congestion is overcrowding that blocks movement; the expressway aims to reduce traffic congestion in the capital.

mcqs.question: What does “legitimate” mean?

options.A: Secret and known to very few people
options.C: Dangerous and likely to cause harm

mcqs.explanation: Legitimate means lawful and accepted as right; the columnist calls peaceful protest a legitimate form of civic participation.

mcqs.question: In the parliament story, what does it mean when a parliament becomes a “rubber stamp”?

options.A: It prints official stamps for government papers
options.B: It moves its office to a new building
options.C: It approves decisions without real debate
options.D: It elects a new Speaker every year

mcqs.explanation: A rubber-stamp parliament formally approves the executive's decisions without real debate or scrutiny; the article says some parliaments became rubber stamps for the executive.

mcqs.question: What is a “free trade agreement”?

options.A: A complete ban on all imports from other countries
options.B: A deal to cut tariffs between countries
options.C: A tax on goods sold inside one country
options.D: A loan from a bank to a trading company

mcqs.explanation: A free trade agreement is a deal between countries to cut tariffs and trade more freely; Vietnam has 17 in force, while Bangladesh has no major one in operation.

mcqs.question: Where and when was COP31 held?
mcqs.explanation: COP31, the 2026 UN Climate Change Conference, was held from 9 to 20 November 2026 in Antalya, Türkiye.

mcqs.question: How much plastic does PRAN-RFL Group recycle each year, according to the editorial?
mcqs.explanation: PRAN-RFL Group recycles approximately 69,000 tonnes of plastic annually; 33,000 tonnes is what Unilever removed from the urban waste stream between June 2022 and April 2026.

mcqs.question: How many Rohingya refugees live in Bangladesh, according to the article?
mcqs.explanation: Among the 1.2 million Rohingya refugees living in Bangladesh, more than half are women and girls.

mcqs.question: How much did Vietnam export in 2025?
mcqs.explanation: In 2025, Vietnam exported $475 billion worth of goods, up 17%; $48 billion is Bangladesh's export figure and $107.75 billion is Vietnam's computers, electronics and components earnings alone.

mcqs.question: How much did Bangladesh import from the United States in FY26?
mcqs.explanation: Imports from the US climbed to $3.6 billion in FY26, up from $2.72 billion the previous fiscal year; $1.29 billion was quarterly imports in April–June.

mcqs.question: What share of Bangladesh's animal protein intake comes from milk, meat and eggs?
mcqs.explanation: Milk, meat and eggs account for 56% of the country's animal protein intake.

mcqs.question: Which article of the Constitution did the Deputy Speaker say should be revised so that MPs can vote more independently?
mcqs.explanation: The Deputy Speaker called for revising Article 70 to ensure MPs can exercise greater independence while retaining safeguards on matters of national interest.

mcqs.question: At which voltages does Power Grid Bangladesh operate its high-voltage network?
mcqs.explanation: Power Grid Bangladesh PLC operates the high-voltage network principally at 132 kV, 230 kV and 400 kV.

mcqs.question: What is the estimated cost of the Dhaka Elevated Expressway project?
mcqs.explanation: The project cost is Tk 89.4 billion; Tk 24.13 billion is the government's viability gap funding and Tk 10.68 billion is what the government has paid so far.

mcqs.question: When was Sheikh Hasina sentenced to death by International Crimes Tribunal-1?
mcqs.explanation: On 17 November 2025, International Crimes Tribunal-1 sentenced her to death in a case involving crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising.

mcqs.question: Which meeting of the India-UAE Joint Defence Cooperation Committee was held in Abu Dhabi?
mcqs.explanation: The agreement was reached at the 14th meeting of the India-UAE Joint Defence Cooperation Committee (JDCC) in Abu Dhabi.

mcqs.question: According to the Air Quality Life Index 2025, how much life expectancy does air pollution cost the average person in Bangladesh?
mcqs.explanation: Bangladesh loses more life expectancy to air pollution than any other country: 5.5 years for the average person.

mcqs.question: Which report highlights the gap between current climate policies and the Paris Agreement's temperature goals?
mcqs.explanation: The United Nations Environment Programme's Emissions Gap Report highlights the continuing gap between current climate policies and the Paris Agreement's temperature goals.
